bias: Financial conditions are being pulled in two directions at once. The Treasury-demand story from earlier in the week held rather than resolved -- the 7Y cleared decently on price (BTC 2.42, dealer 10.76%) but indirect demand stayed thin for a third straight Note auction, and the Treasury module remains at EARLY WARNING. Independently, the bond market kept selling off: the 30Y crossed the 5.5% stress line for the first time this cycle and MOVE pushed above 100. But none of the standard confirmation channels are following -- credit is barely wider, funding is normal, the dollar eased, and equities (including Asia) are broadly higher. That combination reads as a genuine but so-far self-contained rates-market repricing rather than a system-wide liquidity event. The next test is whether credit, funding or equities start reacting to a 30Y above 5.5% and a MOVE above 100, or whether this settles as a one-off term-premium adjustment.

counterargs.read: The evidence continues to point at a rates-market-specific event: the long end has now technically breached the stress line the framework was watching, and bond vol keeps climbing, but every other transmission channel -- credit, funding, USD, and equities -- is calm or improving. That is consistent with a term-premium/real-rate repricing that the rest of the system can absorb, not (yet) a liquidity or credit event. The call is to keep Treasury EARLY WARNING in place (confirmed by three straight thin-indirect Note auctions) without escalating to Intermediation Stress, and to watch whether credit or equities start reacting to a 30Y above 5.5% before revising that read.

treasury_auctions.narrative: The 7Y (91282CRM5, Sep 24) settled decently on the metrics that matter most for dealer stress: BTC 2.42 and dealer take-down 10.76%, both roughly in line with the two comparable 7Y prints in the ledger (Aug 27: BTC 2.50/dealer 10.84%; Jul 28: BTC 2.49/dealer 11.7%). But indirect demand was again soft at 49.13% -- below both those comps (53.72%, 63.0%) and in the same range as the Sep 22 2Y (49.27%) and Sep 23 5Y (46.98%). That makes three straight Note auctions with thinning indirect (often foreign/end-investor) demand, even though only the 5Y also showed elevated dealer take-down. The module holds at EARLY WARNING: this is not a third weak print on every metric (no escalation to Intermediation Stress), but it is not a clean auction either (no downgrade to Healthy). Separately from the auction story, US10Y and US30Y kept selling off into today's session (+11.1bp/+11.7bp since the prior run), with the 30Y crossing the 5.5% long-end stress line for the first time and MOVE spiking a further +9.6% to 104.58. Funding remains normal (SOFR-IORB -2bp, repo_confirmation false) and credit is calm, so this stays short of Intermediation Stress. The next test is the H.8 bank-demand read today and whether credit or equities start reacting to the long end above 5.5%.

transmission.bottom_line: The Treasury-demand story held rather than resolved -- a decent-on-price but soft-on-indirect 7Y keeps the module at Early Warning after three straight thin-indirect Note auctions.
